en: A wheelbarrow is a second-class lever because the heavy load sits between the front wheel, which acts as the fulcrum, and the handles where you apply effort.
A banana peel is exceptionally slippery because it contains microscopic gel-like sacs that burst into a highly lubricating slime when stepped on.
The gravity on the Moon is exactly one-sixth of Earth's gravity, meaning a 60-pound child would weigh only 10 pounds while standing there.
You can permanently demagnetize a magnet by dropping it on the floor, because the physical shock scrambles its neatly aligned internal magnetic domains.
A single bolt of lightning heats the surrounding air to 30,000 degrees Celsius, making it five times hotter than the visible surface of the Sun.
A laser beam bounced off mirrors left on the Moon by Apollo astronauts takes exactly two and a half seconds to return to Earth.
The 1883 eruption of the Krakatoa volcano produced the loudest sound in recorded history, rupturing the eardrums of sailors 40 miles away.
The inner core of the Earth is a solid ball of iron that reaches a scorching 5,400 degrees Celsius, matching the Sun's surface temperature.
A standard AA battery stores roughly 4,000 joules of chemical potential energy, which is enough to lift a one-kilogram textbook 400 meters straight up.
The water at the very bottom of Angel Falls is slightly warmer than at the top because falling converts gravitational potential energy into thermal energy.
A standard clothing zipper works using two tiny inclined planes, called wedges, that force the metal teeth to interlock when you pull the slider.
A piezoelectric crystal inside a barbecue lighter generates a high-voltage electrical spark when struck, converting mechanical kinetic energy directly into electricity.
